context: Current closing price of Dominion Energy (D): $69.99 USD as of 2026-07-21.
justification_text:
My point estimates reflect a modest upward drift from what I assessed as the current price level near $70, with each successive horizon allowing slightly more room for appreciation. At the one-day horizon, the estimate of roughly $70.15 essentially anchors to the prevailing price with minimal expected movement, since short-term crude oil prices tend to mean-revert around recent levels absent a clear directional catalyst. At the one-week horizon, I nudged the estimate slightly higher to $70.40, reflecting a mild underlying bias from supply constraints related to OPEC+ production discipline and seasonal demand patterns. At the one-month horizon, the $71.00 estimate incorporates a somewhat more optimistic demand outlook as refinery runs typically pick up, though I deliberately kept the drift modest given the mixed macroeconomic signals present at the time of the forecast.

The confidence interval widths widen substantially as the horizon extends, which reflects the compounding nature of uncertainty in commodity markets. At one day, the interval is fairly tight because intraday oil price moves rarely exceed one to two percent absent a shock, and the information set changes slowly over hours. By one week, geopolitical noise, inventory report surprises, and currency fluctuations become meaningful contributors to variance, pushing the interval to roughly plus or minus three dollars. At one month, macroeconomic data releases, central bank decisions, and OPEC communication all become live variables, justifying the wider six-dollar band on either side.

Several specific risks could push outcomes outside the stated intervals entirely. On the upside, a significant escalation in Middle East tensions, a surprise OPEC+ production cut announcement, or a sharp draw in U.S. crude inventories could push prices well above $77. On the downside, a weaker-than-expected Chinese demand print, an unexpected loosening of OPEC+ quotas, or a global recession signal could send prices below $65 or even into the low sixties.

It is also worth acknowledging structural uncertainty in my forecast itself. I do not have access to real-time price feeds or breaking news, so my baseline price level could already be stale. If the actual price at the time of reading this has moved meaningfully from the $70 anchor, all three point estimates and intervals should be mentally shifted accordingly. The relative relationships between horizons and the width of the intervals remain the more reliable outputs of this forecast than the absolute dollar levels.
